overview: The Hawaiian Kingdom brought royal government and international diplomacy into conversation with older Hawaiian knowledge and arts. Fishponds show the depth of that inherited environmental engineering; Iolani Palace preserves the setting of the monarchy's later cultural and diplomatic life.

items.text: At Heeia, basalt walls with coral fill control water movement. Sluice gates regulate the mixture of fresh and seawater inside the fishpond.
Brackish water encourages algae, which feed herbivorous fish. Fishponds could provide food when weather made ocean fishing difficult. These practices predate the unified kingdom.
Iolani Palace was completed as a royal residence and a place for official functions and receiving visiting dignitaries.
The palace hosted hula performances and grand balls. Its ceremonial rooms connected performance, hospitality and royal public life.
Liliuokalani succeeded Kalakaua. Her monarchy was subsequently overthrown by the Committee of Safety, which established a provisional government with the American minister's support.
